name: Deputy
tagline: Shift rostering, time clocks, and timesheets for hourly teams, wired through to payroll.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible part of Deputy, a weekly roster grid, a clock-in screen, and a timesheet export, is genuinely a weekend build. The part you are actually paying for is everything downstream of that: turning raw clock data into correctly interpreted pay, with overtime, penalty rates, breaks, and in Australia the specific modern award your staff sit under, then pushing it into payroll without a human re-typing numbers. Get that wrong and you are not shipping a bug, you are underpaying people, which is a legal problem with a paper trail. Add that this is inherently multi-user software your staff must trust on their own phones, and the DIY version collapses into a rostering toy plus a spreadsheet you fix by hand every fortnight. Build the roster if you like, but do not build the pay engine.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where a manager drags shifts onto a weekly roster and staff clock in and out with a PIN, producing a CSV of hours worked per person per pay period.
requirements: A machine or tiny VPS to host it on, reachable from the venue
A shared tablet or kiosk device for clock in and out
Someone willing to hand-calculate pay rules and check every timesheet before payroll
whatYouLose: Award, overtime, and penalty rate interpretation, which is the actual product
Direct payroll integrations, so hours become a manual re-entry job forever
Native staff apps with push notifications, shift swaps, unavailability, and leave requests
Geofenced or photo-verified clock-ins and a defensible audit trail if hours are ever disputed
Someone else's problem when the clock kiosk dies mid-shift on a Saturday night
moatNotes: Award interpretation is the rare feature where being 97 percent correct is worse than not shipping, because the errors are legally actionable and retroactive.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a roster is not the deliverable, correct pay is. Small hospitality and retail operators pay per head to make the chain from clock-in to payslip boring and auditable, and to have a vendor standing behind the rate tables when an employee or a regulator asks how a number was reached. Staff also have to use it, which means it needs to work on their phone, in their language of shift swaps and unavailability, without a manager explaining what a PIN kiosk is. That is a lot of unglamorous surface area to maintain for a business whose real job is selling coffee.
notes: A roster grid and a clock-in button are easy; the rest is labour law and other people's phones. The moat is award and overtime interpretation carried cleanly into payroll, backed by a vendor who is accountable for the rate tables.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted shift roster and time clock for a single small venue. Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, Tailwind. No external services, no accounts system, no telemetry.

Data model: employees (name, hourly rate, active flag, 4 digit PIN hash), shifts (employee id, start, end, role label, notes), punches (employee id, clock_in, clock_out, source).

Screens:
1. /roster : week view, Monday to Sunday, employees as rows, days as columns. Click a cell to add a shift with start time, end time, and role label. Click an existing shift to edit or delete. Copy last week's roster to this week with one button.
2. /kiosk : big touch-friendly screen for a shared tablet. Employee taps their name, enters their PIN, and it toggles clock in or clock out. Show a confirmation with the time and who is currently on shift.
3. /timesheets : pick a date range, show per employee total hours from punches, the variance against rostered hours, and let a manager edit any punch with the original value kept in an edit log. Export CSV: employee, date, clock in, clock out, hours.
4. /employees : basic CRUD, set PIN, set hourly rate, deactivate.

Rules: all times stored UTC, displayed in a single venue timezone set in .env. Unpaid break minutes are a plain manual field on each punch. Gross pay is hours times rate only, and the timesheet page must carry a visible note that no overtime, penalty rates, or award interpretation is applied and pay must be checked by a human before payroll.

Manager pages behind a single shared password from .env via middleware; the kiosk route stays open. Secrets in .env only, with .env.example committed. Ship seed data for 5 employees and one sample week.

Explicitly out of scope: award or overtime engines, payroll API integrations, mobile apps, push notifications, leave and unavailability workflows, shift swapping, geofencing, multi-location.

Deliver a README with setup, backup instructions for the SQLite file, and a short honest list of what this does not do.
